newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Credit Rating downgrades Turkey's debt to BB.
newsitem.headline: Japan Credit Rating downgrades Turkey's debt to BB.

text.p: Japan Credit Rating Agency Ltd (JCR) said on Tuesday it had downgraded yen and euroyen bonds issued by the Republic of Turkey to BB from BB plus and removed them from Credit Monitor.

The JCR said there was concern that if the present solidarity between the pro-Islamic Welfare Party and the centre-right True Path Party was jeopardised, resultant instability might be an obstacle to the achievement of their political and economic goals.
The rating agency said no significant improvement had been seen in Turkey's high inflation rate, which was one of its most persistent problems.
Turkey's consumer price index was expected to rise around 85 percent in 1996, against an earlier projection of 45 percent, it said.
Inertia in high inflation stemmed principally from a huge fiscal deficit caused by structural problems in both the revenue and expenditure sides, JCR said.

A heavy burden of external debt servicing was expected to continue in view of the large medium- and long-term debt repayments totalling around $11 billion for the three years from 1996 and a gradual rise in private-sector debt, it said.

Turkey's overall macroeconomic situation, which is buffeted by inflation, external debt servicing obligations and budget and current account deficits, had been deteriorating despite strong efforts by the government, it said.
